{{Short description|Proposed linguistic universal}}
In [[formal semantics (natural language)|formal semantics]] '''conservativity''' is a proposed [[linguistic universal]] which states that any [[determiner]] <math>D</math> must obey the equivalence <math>D(A,B) \leftrightarrow D(A, A\cap B)</math>. For instance, the [[English language|English]] determiner "every" can be seen to be conservative by the [[logical equivalence|equivalence]] of the following two sentences, schematized in [[generalized quantifier]] notation to the right.<ref name = "cambridgehbk" >{{cite encyclopedia |first1=Westerståhl| last1=Dag|editor-last1=Aloni |editor-first1=Maria|editor1-link=Maria Aloni |editor-last2=Dekker |editor-first2=Paul |encyclopedia=Cambridge Handbook of Formal Semantics |title=Generalized Quantifiers |year=2016 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-1-107-02839-5}}</ref><ref name = "gamut" >{{cite book |last=Gamut |first=L.T.F. |author-link=L.T.F. Gamut |date=1991 |title= Logic, Language and Meaning: Intensional Logic and Logical Grammar |publisher= University of Chicago Press |pages=245–249 |isbn=0-226-28088-8}}</ref><ref name = "barwisecooper" >{{cite journal |last1=Barwise |first1=Jon |last2=Cooper |first2=Robin |date=1981 |title= Generalized Quantifiers and Natural Language |journal=Linguistics and Philosophy |volume=4 |issue=2|pages=159–219 |doi=10.1007/BF00350139 }}</ref>

# Every aardvark bites.   <math>\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \rightsquigarrow every(A,B)</math>
# Every aardvark is an aardvark that bites. <math>\ \ \rightsquigarrow every(A,A\cap B)</math>

Conceptually, conservativity can be understood as saying that the [[element (mathematics)|elements]] of <math>B</math> which are not elements of <math>A</math> are not relevant for evaluating the truth of the [[determiner phrase]] as a whole. For instance, truth of the first sentence above does not depend on which biting non-aardvarks exist.<ref name = "cambridgehbk"/><ref name = "gamut" /><ref name = "barwisecooper" />

Conservativity is significant to semantic theory because there are many logically possible determiners which are not attested as [[denotation]]s of natural language expressions. For instance, consider the imaginary determiner <math>shmore</math> defined so that <math>shmore(A,B)</math> is true iff <math>|A|>|B|</math>. If there are 50 biting aardvarks, 50 non-biting aardvarks, and millions of non-aardvark biters, <math>shmore(A,B)</math> will be false but <math>shmore(A, A\cap B)</math> will be true.<ref name = "cambridgehbk"/><ref name = "gamut" /><ref name = "barwisecooper" />

Some potential counterexamples to conservativity have been observed, notably, the English expression "only". This expression has been argued to not be a determiner since it can stack with bona fide determiners and can combine with non-nominal constituents such as [[verb phrase]]s.<ref>{{cite thesis |last=von Fintel |first=Kai |year=1994 |title= Restrictions on quantifier domains |type=PhD |publisher= University of Massachusetts Amherst}}</ref> 

# Only some aardvarks bite.
# This aardvark will only [<small>VP</small> bite playfully.]

Different analyses have treated conservativity as a constraint on the [[lexicon]], a structural constraint arising from the architecture of the [[syntax-semantics interface]], as well as constraint on [[language acquisition|learnability]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hunter |first1=Tim |last2=Lidz |first2=Jeffrey |year=2013 |title=Conservativity and learnability of determiners|journal=Journal of Semantics |volume=30 |issue=3|pages=315–334 |doi=10.1093/jos/ffs014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Romoli |first1=Jacopo |year=2015 |title=A structural account of conservativity |url= |journal= Semantics-Syntax Interface |volume=2 |issue=1}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1= Steinert-Threlkeld |first1= Shane |last2= Szymanik |first2= Jakub |year=2019 |title=Learnability and semantic universals |journal=Semantics and Pragmatics |volume=12 |issue=4|page= 1 |doi= 10.3765/sp.12.4 |s2cid= 54087074 |doi-access= free |hdl= 11572/364230 |hdl-access= free }}</ref>
